findings.title: Provident Hospital of Cook County temporarily suspended intensive-care-unit operations
findings.publisher: Illinois Health Facilities and Services Review Board / Cook County Health
findings.exact_supporting_passage: on September 20, 2026, Provident temporarily suspended operation of its Intensive Care Unit (“ICU”)
findings.access_consequences: An official Cook County Health notice dated October 16 and publicly posted by Illinois regulators October 21 states Provident suspended its ICU on September 20, 2026, for an anticipated period not exceeding one year. Patients presenting at Provident who require ICU care are to be transferred to John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital of Cook County subject to capacity; additional transfer agreements were being pursued. The notice describes low historic ICU census (1–2 patients per day) and a greater-than-50% reduction in ICU services. This is a HISTORICAL, newly noticed recall candidate, not a new October 25 suspension. Current restoration status not independently verified.
findings.affected_population: Patients in Chicago/Cook County who require inpatient intensive care at Provident Hospital; exact number affected or additional travel burden not established.

coverage_notes.scope: Bounded supplementary recall for high-value healthcare-service losses, EMS/air medical loss, CMS/CLIA actions, and concrete essential-service restorations across U.S. states and territories; not authoritative national collector.
